title: Sprint Manifest — the rails/trains/parallel sequencing artifact
description: Machine-readable sprint plan: the horizontal sequencing within a pass (companion to the vertical Linear tree of ~/.claude/plans/active/subsystem-taxonomy-level-sync-ratchet.md). Emitted by sprint-preflight's brief assembler, AMENDED AND RATIFIED at the operator interview (ratified:false until then), then consumed as the SSOT the conductor composes lifecycle launch args from — hand-typed args are the failure class this artifact retires (the p2 missing-brace launch failure, the p1c invariant drift). DOCTRINE ENCODED, enforced by the generator and the conductor because JSON Schema cannot express topology: [R-rails] for every phase P and every entry in P.contracts_consumed, the owner must appear STRICTLY EARLIER in `sequence` or already exist on trunk — consumed-before-owned is a topological violation and a generation-time HALT (this check catches seam conflicts that file-overlap analysis cannot: both M6 DECISION-NEEDED halts — deckPlan ownership drift, recap-through-promotion — were of this class). [R-door] a contract with kind:'door' (schemas, wire formats, error envelopes, ID schemes — the one-way-door list) is owned by the EARLIEST feasible phase and carries frozen_after:true; later phases consume, never redefine (M6's 'shapes freeze again after p3b' discovered this rule three times ad hoc). [R-hub] every file appearing in two or more touch_sets is a hub file and must be OWNED by exactly one phase; other touchers acquire a conflict edge driving serial order. [R-train] among phases with no rail relation, land order is ASCENDING conflict footprint (least→most merge-conflict risk): the disruptive branch lands LAST, so its conflicts are resolved once, by the branch that caused them, against a settled base — this minimizes total expected rebase work and concentrates resolution at the point of maximum information. [R-parallel] phases with zero conflict edges of either type may share a parallel_group (the CALM cut: disjoint implementation is monotone and coordination-free; trunk integration is non-monotone and stays serial). [R-mode] parallel_group is only honored when every member has mode:'ratchet' — tracer-bullet phases run agent-serial by doctrine (unproven slices earn no parallelism). [R-cost] every phase carries cost_class (FM one-way-door 5): build = cites a work item and produces a persisted artifact (the default for sprint phases); serve = fulfills an external run; defense = neither.

sprint.description: Human name, e.g. 'M6 deck — p4a..p5b remainder'

verified_at.description: The stamped HEAD every premise was probed against; refreshed at ceremony when the base moves

registry.description: Path to the invariant registry read fresh at every launch (invariants/gates/policy stay single-source THERE, never here)

generated_by.description: Engine + run id that emitted this, e.g. 'sprint-preflight wf_xxx'

ratified.description: false = draft awaiting the operator interview; the conductor may only launch from a ratified manifest

merge_topology.description: Prose statement of the integration shape, e.g. 'stacked phase branches → squash onto milestone baseline → merge --no-ff into dev'

sequence.description: The ratified TOTAL ORDER of phase ids: rails first (descending contract fan-out), then trains ascending conflict footprint; parallel groups appear as consecutive entries sharing parallel_group

issues.description: Tracker ids for the phase (Linear, team FOR). PORT NOTE (entropic-substrate-lm, 2026-09-17): the Linear project "entropic-substrate-lm — hexagonal refactor" now exists (one milestone per phase, one issue per planned commit branch), so the upstream minItems:1 constraint is restored; the 2026-08-12 port had dropped it because no project existed then.

mode.description: tracer = unproven slice (timeboxed, circuit-breaker, agent-serial); ratchet = known set (parallel-eligible)

liveDeferred.description: If the live gate is conductor-deferred, the reason and re-certification owner — an honest deferral is recorded, never a false green

model_tier.description: Fleet model policy for this phase's launch, e.g. 'opus-only variant per operator ruling'

kind.description: door = one-way-door class (schema/wire-format/envelope/ID) — earliest feasible owner, frozen after

frozen_after.description: true = no later phase may redefine; amendments require a conductor ruling recorded in the registry

touch_set.description: Files/globs this phase edits — the input to hub detection and R-train footprint

type.description: file = shared touch-set (train risk); contract = owned/consumed relation (rail dependency)

evidence.description: The shared files or the contract name — never a bare assertion

resolution.description: How the sequence resolves this edge

parallel_group.description: Non-null = forked-impl-heads eligible with same-group phases (R-parallel + R-mode both required)

engine_mode.description: Launcher-read lifecycle engine mode, copied VERBATIM into args.phase.mode by the composer (wave-args --manifest <file> --phase <id>). Distinct from mode (tracer|ratchet = sequencing). arch = Opus design gate + direct Sonnet TDD; normal = Sonnet director -> haiku packets; direct = the plain serial spine: direct Sonnet TDD, no recon, no design gate — the former td-phase-lifecycle.js topology. REQUIRED and arch whenever the phase owns any kind:door contract (see if/then). Absent = the composer refuses to launch (never a default).

lifecycle.description: Sprint lifecycle (operator-ruled 2026-07-29, D12): queued = ratified, awaiting first launch; active = phases in flight; archived = sprint complete. ROTATION PROTOCOL: at the NEXT sprint's prelaunch commit, the completed sprint's manifest flips to archived and is renamed sprint-manifest.<slug>.json, and its launch-queue.jsonl rotates to launch-queue.<slug>.jsonl — the active filenames always hold exactly one sprint, so the final no-ff merge into dev never conflicts on ledger history and concerns never mix across sprints.

ledger.description: Path of this sprint's launch-queue ledger file (rotates with the manifest per the lifecycle protocol)
